It's not so much that deflection is too strong (although obviously way
better than any other bounce card). It's more that dominate gives you
the strongest offense and strongest defense in the game. Dementation
has become more popular because with CE on, it's hard to get DOM/OBF
on reasonable sized vampires. But with bleed being the primary
offense in the game, and one discipline giving you both the best
offense and the best defense to bleed, it's completely unbalanced. If
Deflection had been, say, a Chimerstry card, I doubt there would be as
much uproar over it (and don't think it's just started now, 15 years
after printing - it's always been true and always been complained
about).

Now, the situation with DOM being the best discipline has definitely
improved, because other disciplines have gotten some pretty good
cards, and dominate has gotten almost nothing in recent sets (dating
back years). Govern the Unaligned, while it still looks overpowered,
no longer completely defines dominate. Quietus has Loss (though it
doesn't have the bloat potential), Serpentis has Eternal Mask (though
it's closer to Kine Dominance than to GtU), Camera Phone and Leverage
have powered up disciplineless bleed, etc., etc... And Presence was
always pretty close to Dominate in bleed, trading a little bleed
potential for more bloat potential, and Public Trust and Dream World
have brought them even closer. But DOM is still the best offense, and
Deflection is still the best defense. I like the idea of a) making
anti-bounce more accessible, but to odd disciplines or combinations of
disciplines (I don't think Dem really needed it); and b) creating more
non-Dom bounce.

Messages.Body:
Bounce is an issue.

Why is a bounce so effective?

A. It reduces a bleed against you to zero.
B. It gives you the opportunity to hurt your prey (other opponent) in
someone others turn.
C. Minimal risk.

Lets start with A. When you for example are being bled for 6, then it
becomes clear that it is a huge bleed reduction card, which (in
general) doesn't cost that much more than a specialized bleed
reduction card, but is more effective. Most bleed reduction cards just
prevent 2 to 3 pool maximum. Compare it with that beautiful card "Keep
it Simple" (why why why does that one cost 1 blood), bounces are much
more effective. The main advantage bleed reducers have over bounce
cards is when only two players are left.

Advantage B. Not only does it reduce a bleed against you, but also you
can hurt another player with that bleed. Instead of that 6 pool loss,
I can take 6 pool from my prey. And it isn't even in my turn. At the
moment the card to watch is Enkil Cog, which give you an extra action
during the turn of someone else. Well a bounce does have similarities.

Advantage C. The main risk is that you are left with two players and
that the bounce cards became useless. However a lot of bounce cards do
have a second function. Another risk is that it will be bounced back
(but hey you have to bounce it in the first place).
Furthermore there tend to be cards that target bounces, like "Two
Wrongs" and "Narrow Mind" to name a few. But it is still pretty safe
to use bounce.

That is why a lot of my decks have a Dominate or Auspex module to be
able to bounce. Vampires are added to the Crypt that have nothing in
common with the main theme of the deck. Dominate and Auspex cards are
added that can't be used by most vampires in your Crypt. I don't call
that a good balance.

Ironically a lot of cards that could replace bounce cards like
intercept and bleed reducers are again Auspex cards.

In most cases I will support the thought that the disciplines should
keep their own characteristics. I was not happy with the KoT cards
"Rego Motus" and "Old Friends" for example. But for bounce my personal
view is different. There should be more disciplines with bounce
abilities and there should also be more ways to prevent it. Maybe anti
bounce tech should be a characteristic of some disciplines.

A nice attempt was being made with "Lost in Translation", but it has
to many disadvantages and therefore you will only find it once or so
in the TWDA. You want to bounce bleeds as soon as possible. So you
bring out weenies that can bounce. Weenies cannot use LiT very
effectively.

There should be more anti-bounce cards, but design them in such a way
that they are still useful to some extend in case only two players are
left. When such cards are available then there won't be any reason to
ban cards like Deflection (by far the best bounce card).

H

> I cant belive people want to keep bounce as primary bleed defence ...

Without bounce, S+B becomes simply unbearably powerful. Because other
defenses against S+B generally aren't efficient enough (bleed reduction;
-2 bleed per card is simply not effective enough of a defense against
significant bleed offense) or viable to back up decks that can reliably
win games (rush and intercept; both of which can be very good at
stopping S+B, but to be good enough at that, you often aren't good
enough at actually being able to oust anyone). Bounce means that
bleeding for 5 at +4 stealth all the time has a drawback (you might oust
someone other than your prey) as opposed to being a virtually certain
path towards victory. As the game exists now, it needs bleed bounce to
exist.

This could have been circumvented from the beginning, but it wasn't, so
here we are. The only way to do away with bounce all together is to
invent some other kind of almost as certain bleed defense--maybe super
bleed reduction (something along the lines of pay one blood to make a
bleed action fail, except this sort of thing removes the risk associated
with being bounced when bleeding for 5 at +4 stealth and is probably too
safe, as when you bounce a bleed at someone, there is always the chance
that they'll bounce it back at you) or whatever.

The only problem with Deflection is that it is far and away more
powerful than all the other bounce cards--Telepathic Misdirection, My
Enemy's Enemy, Redirection, LiiT, Murmur all have significant
complications attached to them. Telepathic is nice and flexible and can
bounce anyone, but you need AUS which isn't hard in an AUS based deck
(as AUS weenies are pretty easy to find) but difficult to slot in. MEE
has the same issues as Telepathic, but then also bounces to someone you
don't want to bounce too. Redirection requires you to bounce a younger
vampire (and not ally) or have DOM and still tap anyway. LiiT has all
sorts of drawbacks, and is really only suitable for decks that have huge
vampires that don't have AUS or dom (which doesn't actually come up all
that often if you want to work it out). Murmur is also nice and
flexible, but even at DOM it is just like inferior Redirection.
Deflection, as a bleed defense, is just far and away the best there
is--no disadvantages, no limitations, can be played by any random 2 cap
with dom and bounce that bleed of 7 from Arika. At superior, you don't
tap (when *all* of the other bounce cards tap you for playing it) so you
can keep playing them. Deflection is stupidly powerful.

Is this horrible? No, not really--I'm ok with bleed defense being better
than bleed. Except that the bleed defense that *is* better than bleed is
incredibly narrow; it is just Deflection. Which makes all the other
bleed defenses less attractive. And makes Dominate just too damn good.

> First, they bitch about how big capers need to have Auspex or
> Dominate, and second they want to keep status quo. Geez, that is sick.

There isn't a way to fix the status quo. 'Cause the status is not, uh,
quo. Without completely retooling the game.

> I support:
>
> (3) More anti-bounce tech

Which just makes S+B more powerful. S+B is *still* the most effective
deck strategy. I'm totally ok with people being able to oust their prey
reliably, but it is also good to be able to compete defensively.

> (6) Make alternative (non bounce) solution 'worth it'

With Deflection existing, there isn't really a way to do this. What kind
of reliable bleed defense can you come up with that is a single card and
costs 1 blood and can be played by an inferior discipline that is going
to be competitive with Deflection *and* balanced?

The problem with "reduce bleed by 1" is that it simply isn't worth it.
Spending a card and having an untapped minion (or another card) to
save 1 pool is a bad trade off. The general model across the board
seems to be "gain 2 pool for a single, free card" (see: Art Scam,
Enchant Kindred, Scouting Mission, Kahbar: Leadership or whatever, the
new one where you gain 2 for being an 8 cap, etc.). Yeah, the ones
that are actions have the cost of having to take an action. Which
seems roughly equivalent, for my money, to the cost of having to be
bled and be untapped. That all those numerous attempts at bleed
reduction cards default to "reduce by 1" makes these cards generally
not that useful.

Reducing a bleed by 2 is almost worth it, so Telepathic Counter
actually sees play once and a while--if bleed reduction cards had
multiple uses, a bleed reduction of 2 would be good (as the reduction
of opportunity cost would make up for the card generally not being as
good as bounce). Looking at the currently viable bleed reduction
cards:

-Telepathic Counter: Completely useless if you aren't being bled, so
has a reasonably high opportunity cost (like all the cards that only
reduce bleeds). On the upside, if you have AUS, you can reduce bleeds
by 2 over and over for free. On the downside, if you have AUS, you
should probably be playing Telepathic Misdirection. Still, sees play
occasionally.

-Truth in Ink: A nice card as it reduces by 2 for free. Is also
useless if you aren't being bled, but can be played by any BH vampire,
so easy to use. It not being able to use it against another BH vampire
comes up once and a while, but not enough to make the card useless
(unless you are playing SoC draft...). Sees play occasionally.

-Friend of Mine (for): It reduces by 2 at for, which is good, but
costs a blood, which is bad. And you need to be an Anarch. So I
suspect that it would be a good and reasonable card if it was free
(see: Detect Authority). I use it a lot, but that is me. I rarely see
anyone else ever use it (except for Darbo! Go Darbro!)

-Detect Authority: Free and reduces by 2, so good! But as it comes
from Tha, you probably have reliable AUS or dom, so you are probably
using bounce instead.

-Nest of Eagles: Can reduce a reasonable number of bleeds (allies and
vamps 5 and smaller, which is a lot of them) by 3, so can be
excellent. The rest of the time, only reduces bleeds by 1, which isn't
good. But can be played by any Assamite, so easy to play. Useless if
you aren't being bled. Not a bad card. Sees some amount of play.

-Steadfastness: A weird card which is interesting in that it gives
fortitude intercept and the ability to reduce a bleed by 1. I'd much
rather have seen it reduce a bleed by 2, at which point it becomes a
strong card, instead of a "might see play once and a while" card.

-Ancestor's Insight: In theory, good, as it has the two uses (+1 bleed
or reduce a bleed by 1). But as the reduce by 1 is inferior auspex,
and the +1 bleed is superior, it isn't great for defense and isn't
great for offense. If it had been +1 bleed at inferior and reduce by 2
at superior, it would be strong but not game breaking. As it is, the
Laibons who can play it kind of blow most of the time, so dubious.

There are a few others, but they are all generally worse that the
above ones. Most of them kind of fall down in the "Actually useful"
category, due to the opportunity cost and/or only reducing by 1 a lot
of the time. If there were "inf: foo that is generally useful like
press/+1 stealth/whatever; SUP: reduce bleed by 2.", in non Auspex/
Dominate disciplines, we'd see more bleed reduction, which would be
good. Steadfastness is almost there. But the reduction of 1 just isn't
worth including it for the reduction, so if you are including it, you
generally want to try the Intercept, so the bleed reduction isn't
likely to see much play.

-Peter

The thing that a lot of people miss about Telepathic Counter (and this
applies to some of the other examples as well), is that while
Telepathic Misdirection is far better against a single bleed, TC
becomes more card-efficient the more bleeds you have to deal with.
Most effective is when you have access to both kinds of defense.

As the number of bleeds increases, the "cost" of having to leave a
minion untapped to play reduction decreases (you only have to have one
minion untapped to play a bunch of reduction cards). Effective defense
when the bleeds are spread out uses fewer card slots and costs fewer
blood than bounce. Better still, if you can see the last bleed coming,
you can bounce that one and take advantage of the wild efficiency of
bounce against a single bleed. You also get to take advantage of the
psychology of making your predator feel like only a bleed of 3+ will
actually land while you're prepping to bounce, making it even more
effective, which is why you almost never see pure-TC decks, but you do
see decks with TC + TM, sometimes with large numbers of TC, even
though they own plenty of TM and bounce is "better" than reduction.

-witness1

The point that I don't think you're addressing and I agree with is
that Telepathic Counter uses a lot less in resources than Telepathic
Misdirection. If you leave 1 guy untapped, then you can play N-1
TC's, and 1 TM, without requiring a Wake. Each Wake-type card that
you would tend to use with TM has its drawbacks. Forced Awakening
will make the bounce cost a second blood, WWEF won't be replaced until
your untap phase, Filip is only once per bigger minion you have, and
On the Qui Vive is once per time around the table. Eluding the Arms
of Morpheus works similarly to Forced in this scenario, although it
does require a block attempt, which would potentially be a bad thing,
depending on the circumstance. Eyes of Argus is almost certainly the
best card to use, though it's not useful as a Wake for inferior auspex
minions (who, I admit, couldn't play TC to full effect or TM to
bounce), and even decks with lots of Eyes might go with another backup
Wake for instances when you want to use Eyes for intercept.

Regardless of which cost you choose to go with for your Wake card, it
still means that Telepathic Misdirection costs you a blood and an
untapped minion. If you had but 1 untapped minion, then each TM after
the first costs a blood and 2 cards instead of 1 card. I think that
in a very real way, unless you are getting bled for at least 4 per
action (which is not exactly rare, but isn't, IMHO, nearly as common
as getting bled for 3 or less), then playing 2 or 3 TC's and 1 TM
during your predator's turn tends to get you better results than
playing 3 or 4 TM's and 2 or 3 Wakes. Saving a blood is almost
(depending again on circumstance) as good as saving a pool.

Most decks can't do everything. Yeah, a weenie AUS deck or a serious
wall deck can do things like plan on playing a Telepathic Counter on
the first bleed, and then blocking the next bleed, and then bouncing a
third big bleed. But decks that can do that are pretty few and far
between. Most decks tend to pick and choose their defenses--they have
enough room for their offense, and then they build in some sort of
defense option. Which often will be a handful of bounce cards, a
handful of wakes, and a couple Delaying Tactics or something. 'Cause
more often than not, your offense takes up a lot of space, and
spending too much space on defense keeps you alive and but makes you
lose.

So yeah, in an optimal situation where you are a weenie AUS deck and
have tons of space alloctaed to defense, and can both block bleeds,
reduce bleeds and bounce bleeds, then yeah, the Counter is going to
look strong. But again, I don't think this is most decks. Most decks
bleed defense is along the lines of 8-10 bounce cards and some wakes,
as that is all their is realistically space for. In a deck like this
(which strikes me as far more of an average than something that can
bounce and reduce and block all at the same time), having, like, 4
Telepathic Counters and 4 Telepathic Misdirection is going to be
better than just 8 Telepathic Misdirections rarely. And most of the
time, it is just going to be worse.

Sure. I can certainly see situations where having the mix of Counters
and Misdirections are going to pay off and be great. But that isn't
going to be "most of the time". It is going to be a "once in a while,
in the occasional clever deck that can pull it off".

-Peter
